description: Thick, red, rimmed with brown fat. Which beast it came off is between you, the cook, and nobody else.
lore: Hunger here is a habit rather than a need, which makes ten gold of meat the strangest purchase in the trade: you are not buying food, you are buying three hours. A slab that size wants turning, and a spit wants somebody sat at it, and people who would never sit down for a telling will sit down for a plate.

[[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] buys the biggest she can afford rather than the best, for exactly that reason. [[lore/the_waking|The newly woken]] come up off the grass unable to give their own names and most of them want to walk off into the dark and be elsewhere; a person holding a plate stays where they are for as long as it takes to eat it, which is generally long enough for someone to ask them one true thing. The cooking is the courtesy. The meat is only how it gets paid for.
gm_notes: The cheapest junk on the list doing the most important work in the setting. Use it whenever a fire scene needs a reason for people to stay put; the meadow fire's meat budget is a real line in Solveig's week.
